channel.title: Daily Byte
channel.description: A byte-size daily digest for engineers who value depth over noise. — edition 2026-09-16

item.title: Tell agents the why, not just the how
item.description: Early AI agents required precise step-by-step instructions, but modern frontier models fail differently—making incorrect assumptions about the user's goals or priorities rather than misunderstanding the task. The author illustrates this with GPT-6-Astra, which produces minified code unless explicitly told that humans will be reading it. The main advice is to give agents broad context about priorities and goals, not just specific technical specs. A sample prompt for a project called Deckard shared the author's long-term aim of building a tool to hide AI content on web pages, short-term goals around running an AI detection model efficiently on a MacBook, personal context, and even initial guesses about which models might work—half of which was broad context. For work, the author writes a paragraph explaining relative priorities among bug-avoidance, observability, elegance, and performance, explicitly noting which can be traded off. Treating agents as expert advisors without supplying necessary context is compared to committing the XY problem.

item.title: GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: Using the diff, terminal, and browser
item.description: The GitHub Copilot app now includes built-in diff, terminal, and browser panels, allowing users to review, run, and preview agent-generated code without switching between separate applications. The diff panel displays added lines in green and removed lines in red, letting users accept changes, leave comments, or request further modifications. The terminal panel enables running project commands directly within the session, including dev server scripts, and supports multiple terminal windows simultaneously. For projects with a user interface, the browser panel allows users to open and test features, using the Pick & Polish tool to select specific elements and iterate with the agent. This side-by-side workflow lets users verify what changed, confirm the code runs, and validate functionality before accepting the agent's work and creating a pull request.

item.title: GitHub availability report: August 2026
item.description: In August 2026, GitHub experienced five incidents that degraded performance across its services, with the two most significant occurring on August 6 (a roughly 10-hour GitHub Actions outage affecting 74+ organizations) and August 17 (a roughly 7.5-hour incident impacting Issues, pull requests, APIs, Copilot, and authentication, with about 29,000 organizations seeing failures). Both incidents stemmed from capacity limits being exceeded during routine deployments or traffic peaks, compounded by service mesh scaling failures and client retry behavior that amplified the problems. Despite these setbacks, GitHub made progress on its Azure migration, running production MySQL primaries in Azure for the first time and achieving up to 64.3% read traffic from migrated services. Capacity and reliability improvements included moving the 24-table authentication-core cohort off the oldest shared database, removing about one million queries per second, and reducing GitHub Actions peak cache CPU utilization from 98% to 80% through job-routing changes.

item.title: Marketing ops as code: Automating events from planning to follow-up on GitHub
item.description: If you can write down how you do your work, you can automate it. Here's what I did to support GitHub's APAC marketing team. The post Marketing ops as code: Automating events from planning to follow-up on GitHub appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

item.title: Intrinsic Robot Rewarding: Reusing VLA Representations for Autonomous Evaluation and Policy Improvement
item.description: Intrinsic Robot Rewarding (IRR) proposes reusing the visual representations and demonstration data already available in vision-language-action (VLA) systems to evaluate robotic outcomes and provide feedback for policy improvement. Successful demonstration endpoints define task-specific references, while the policy's frozen visual encoder provides the feature space in which new outcomes are assessed. The core reward mechanism adds a reference bank and scoring operation to the existing pipeline, eliminating the need for a separate learned evaluator or additional perception backbone. This approach aims to reduce integration effort, enable efficient reward computation, and minimize recurring human outcome scoring. The authors demonstrate the concept on an operational COMAU Racer 3 robot at technology readiness level 4 (TRL 4), presenting the reward formulation, central research questions, and an evaluation methodology linking reward reliability to task success and supervision effort. The intended contribution is a reusable framework for learning and improvement from data already present in industrial robot systems.

item.title: High-Fidelity Digital Twin Data Models by Randomized Dynamic Mode Decomposition and Deep Learning with Applications in Fluid Dynamics
item.description: Diana A. Bistrian presents a framework for creating high-fidelity digital twin data models (DTMs) from numerical code outputs using non-intrusive techniques that do not require Galerkin projection of governing equations onto a reduced modes basis. The DTM is defined as a reduced-complexity model that mirrors the original process behavior, reproducing dynamics at lower CPU time and hardware costs while maintaining high accuracy. The proposed methodology combines randomized dynamic mode decomposition with deep learning artificial intelligence to produce outputs consistent with the original source data. The framework was validated on three shock wave phenomena of increasing complexity in numerical simulation. A thorough assessment was conducted to evaluate the performance of the new digital twin data models in terms of numerical accuracy and computational efficiency. The work was published in Modelling 2022, volume 3, issue 3, pages 314–332.

item.title: Bio-Inspired Palette Evolution in Indirectly Encoded Substrates: Timescale Compatibility Shapes Activation Function Discovery
item.description: This paper tackles meta-learning of activation function palettes for indirectly encoded neural networks by designing 13 evolutionary strategies, 11 inspired by biological adaptation mechanisms alongside baseline and oracle controls. Each strategy translates a biological principle into an operator—for instance, circadian-inspired oscillatory gating cycles functions in and out of the palette on a fixed schedule, while immune-inspired Clonal Selection permanently protects functions correlated with fitness. Across more than 3,000 runs on parity and non-parity problems, plus an independent replication with new seeds, bio-inspired strategies matched the tuned baseline's solve rate while converging up to twice as fast, with the Circadian strategy halving total compute. The central finding is that timescale compatibility governs success: strategies whose characteristic timescale matches the evolutionary evaluation window consistently outperform those operating too slowly. Rankings also reversed across problem types, indicating no single strategy dominates all domains, though rescaling the slowest strategy bypassed the oscillatory barrier entirely, with all nine parity solutions using non-oscillatory activations paired with min or max aggregation.

item.title: Neuro-Symbolic Hierarchical Intention Anticipation in Human Behavior
item.description: Researchers from LISSI propose a neuro-symbolic framework for anticipating human goals before an observed behavior is complete, formulated as goal inference from partially observed multimodal episodes combined with structured prediction of the remaining behavior. A compact Hierarchical Planning Decoder is attached to a frozen neuro-symbolic recognition encoder and predicts the next actions, remaining activities, low-level intentions, and episode high-level intention across four ontological levels. Training uses soft neuro-symbolic regularization combining transition-coherence and hierarchical continuity losses, while inference applies hard reachability masks to enforce ontological validity. On a benchmark of 15,002 multimodal episodes built over NTU RGB+D 120 features, the advantage over the strongest sequential baseline grows with the anticipation horizon, rising from +1.7 points at step 1 to +7.3 points at step 3 in top-5 accuracy. Under compositional generalization with one held-out parent association, this lead expands to +4.9 points at step 1, while 96.8% of anticipated trajectories satisfy joint logic constraints compared to 88.1% for the strongest baseline and a 73.9% ground-truth floor. Soft logic terms alone cut HLI-reachability violations by 59.8 to 71.1% relative, and the hard masks eliminate them entirely.

item.title: Optimization over covariance matrices with a parameterized metric
item.description: The choice of Riemannian metric can strongly influence the convergence of gradient-based optimization over covariance matrices. Euclidean, Bures-Wasserstein and affine-invariant metrics are common choices, but their relative effectiveness depends on the objective. We introduce a two-parameter family defined by $X^{p}LX^{q}+X^{q}LX^{p}=U$, solved for $L$ at each tangent vector $U$, that contains all three as exact members, at $(0,0)$, $(1,0)$ and $(1,1)$, and extends past them. We treat the choice of member as a particular way of preconditioning for a given problem. To this end, we analyze the conditioning of the Riemannian Hessian at the solution. item.title: OpenArm: An open-source 7DOF humanoid arm
item.description: OpenArm is an open-source 7DOF humanoid arm designed for physical AI research and deployment in contact-rich environments, featuring high backdrivability and compliance for safe human-robot interaction. It offers human-scale proportions and practical payload capabilities, with a complete bimanual system priced at $6,500 USD. The platform supports teleoperation, imitation learning, simulation, and real-world data collection across various research applications. OpenArm Cell provides a standardized environment with unified background, lighting, and camera placement, enabling reproducible research conditions worldwide. The project includes multiple repositories covering hardware CAD files, URDF descriptions, CAN control, ROS2 integration, teleoperation, Isaac Lab and MuJoCo simulations, datasets, and Dora dataflow nodes. Hardware is licensed under CERN-OHL-S-2.0 while software components use Apache-2.0.

item.title: Show HN: An e-ink frame that hears birds and draws them as 1800s illustrations
item.description: Fugleramme is an open-source e-ink frame that uses a Raspberry Pi to detect birds by audio and render them as hand-curated 1800s illustrations on an Inky Impression panel. It polls BirdNET-Go, a local AI classifier, and matches each species to one of over 800 cut-outs from real public-domain natural-history plates covering more than 400 species. Detected birds are arranged on a textured paper page, sized by body mass, with the display only refreshing when the bird list changes. The project works in web-only mode as well, and includes an admin page for configuration, automatic updates, and Docker or scripted installation. A live demo runs from the creator's kitchen window in Bergen, Norway, and prebuilt frames are available on request.

item.title: Show HN: Ordewell – turn one goal into an ordered plan of coding-agent tasks
item.description: Ordewell is a tool that converts a single development goal into an ordered plan of coding-agent tasks, each carrying its own runner, model, thinking effort, and mode, all editable before any tokens are spent. The planner researches the workspace read-only, asks clarifying questions when the goal is vague, and delivers the plan as its final message in a persistent chat session. Tasks execute in real coding-agent sessions following a dependency graph, and a task only completes when a unique completion marker appears in its runner's output, with exit code kept as diagnostic evidence. Built-in runners include Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode, which can serve as the planner on their own subscriptions without a separate API key, while 25 additional providers are supported via their respective keys. The same core is exposed through a VS Code extension, a tmux-based terminal UI, and a scriptable CLI, and custom runners can be added through plugin manifests.

item.title: WangNet – 1.8 MB, zero-dependency Numberwang adjudication in 11 languages
item.description: WangNet is a 1.8 MB neural network stored as a JSON file that adjudicates whether numbers are Numberwang, requiring only Python 3.8 or newer with zero external dependencies. The roughly 100-line inference code runs without PyTorch or NumPy, reading characters directly through an embedding, two convolutional layers, and linear layers totaling 80,804 parameters. It supports 11 languages, accepts digits, words, arithmetic expressions, Roman numerals, and ordinals, and produces four verdicts ranging from "not Numberwang" to "Wangernumb!" On 486 held-out adjudications the model achieves 88.9% accuracy with a macro-F1 of 0.896, though arithmetic on unseen operands remains its weak spot at 44–72%. A hosted demo runs on Hugging Face Spaces using gradio, which is only needed for the interface and not the model itself.

item.title: iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27
item.description: Apple's iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, and other platform updates introduce Siri AI, a more capable and conversational assistant powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence, featuring personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, and integration across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro. New Apple Intelligence features enhance Photos with Spatial Reframing, Extend, and an upgraded Clean Up tool, while Image Playground now supports photorealistic styles and the SynthID standard for identifying AI-generated images. Safari gains tab organization, website change notifications, and custom extension creation, and Call Context surfaces relevant information during business calls. Updated parental controls and a redesigned Screen Time experience offer easier child account setup, age-based safeguards, Ask to Browse for Safari, enhanced Communication Safety for violent content, and daily time allowances for entertainment, games, and social media. Platform-wide improvements include faster performance, smoother cellular-to-Wi-Fi transitions, refined search capabilities, and Liquid Glass design updates with personalization options.

item.title: I can't stop thinking about Papua New Guinea
item.description: Papua New Guinea hosts nearly 1,000 distinct languages and was home to roughly a million people living undiscovered in its highlands until 1930, when Australian Mick Leahy stumbled upon them while prospecting for gold. People first arrived on the island around 50,000 years ago, and highland communities became effectively isolated from the coast about 10,000 years ago when agriculture developed there independently. New Guineans cultivated taro, bananas, and sugarcane, with bananas and sugarcane first domesticated on the island, eventually spreading worldwide. Because root vegetables spoiled quickly and highlanders lacked draft animals and writing, tribes never formed larger centralized societies, leaving small groups of a few hundred people in constant warfare and largely unable to travel or trade safely with neighbors. These encounters between isolated highlanders and outsiders were captured in thousands of photos and hours of film, and are detailed in the book "First Contact" along with a documentary built from Leahy's original footage.

item.title: 25 years of mass surveillance is enough
item.description: Following the September 11, 2001 attacks, the U.S. government shifted from targeted surveillance to mass techniques including the NSA's bulk telephone records collection and the Upstream program. The USA Freedom Act in 2015 ended some indiscriminate collection, but Section 702 surveillance continues until at least 2027. Mass surveillance has expanded beyond intelligence agencies to law enforcement like ICE, private companies such as Google and Facebook, and technologies including Flock license plate readers and facial recognition, with FBI Director Kash Patel confirming the agency purchases information from data brokers. This shift raises Fourth Amendment concerns, allowing government access to personal data without individualized suspicion, probable cause, or particularized descriptions of what is being seized. Despite occasional claims of success, the national security community has never provided comprehensive analysis demonstrating these programs effectively prevent attacks or make people safer.
